Outbreak reproduction ratio

Source: R/core.R
r_ob.Rd

For Poisson offspring, implements Eq. (3) and the below-threshold continuation in Eqs. (20)–(26) of Wang and Valdano (2026). For supercritical irreducible matrices, the stable expression crossprod(R, p) / p is used. For subcritical or critical irreducible primitive matrices, the Perron–Frobenius continuation is the spectral radius for every community. An irreducible but periodic matrix can lack the required generation-by-generation limit and is reported explicitly. Diagonal matrices reduce community-by-community to diag(R).

Usage

r_ob(R, p = NULL, offspring = "poisson", omega = 0)

Arguments

R

A finite, nonnegative square reproduction matrix. R[i, j] is the expected number of infections in destination i caused by one infected individual from source j.

p

Optional outbreak-probability vector. If supplied, it must match the maximal fixed-point solution and, when named, the matrix identifiers.

offspring

Offspring distribution. Either "poisson" (the default) or "nb" for independent negative-binomial counts on directed edges.

omega

A finite nonnegative scalar overdispersion parameter. For the negative-binomial model, size = 1 / omega and Var(X[i,j]) = R[i,j] * (1 + omega * R[i,j]). The value zero recovers the Poisson model. Heterogeneous dispersion matrices are unsupported.

Value

A named numeric vector of outbreak reproduction ratios.

Details

For independent negative-binomial counts on directed edges, implements Eq. (S4) of the S1 Appendix. This expression is derived directly from the conditional-expectation definition of the outbreak reproduction ratio. The publication does not establish a negative-binomial continuation when an outbreak probability is zero, so that regime is rejected explicitly.

General reducible, non-diagonal matrices are unsupported for the Poisson continuation because the published result assumes irreducibility; no component convention is imposed by this package.

Examples

R <- matrix(c(1.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.8), 2, byrow = TRUE,
            dimnames = list(c("A", "B"), c("A", "B")))
r_ob(R)
#>        A        B 
#> 1.365432 1.162687
